note: Claims-first draft register for Spec 035, generated alongside spec.md from the PRED-2026-010 registration in docs/PREDICTION_REGISTER.md (registered 2026-10-13) and its derivation record (reports/pred010_derivation_record.json), under the owner's draft order of 2026-10-20. claims.text: A verdict under Spec 035 states whether the registered criterion for PRED-2026-010 is met, and nothing beyond that statement.
claims.boundary: Scope claim for the whole spec. The registered prediction (docs/PREDICTION_REGISTER.md, PRED-2026-010) is the input, not a question; a verdict is a statement about the registered criterion on the registered data. It does not govern the step-0 checks (C04-C06, C09), the computation (C10-C11), or the register handling (C14). What the signs mean, why they pattern as they do, and stability at any other site are never judged under this spec.
alternatives: A scored prediction may be read as evidence about the script's decipherment or about sign meanings.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 outcome statement claiming more than the registered criterion's outcome on the registered data defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A scored prediction may be read as evidence about the script's decipherment or about sign meanings.
metadata.verdict_rule: A Spec 035 product makes a criterion statement only.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C01 states this spec's scope (the registered criterion's outcome); C13 states the verdict wording's permitted independence claim and its required caveat. The two govern different objects - this study's outputs, and the wording of those outputs - and are consistent by construction: a verdict inside scope is exactly one whose wording claims only what C13 permits. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: The success criterion is the registered one: at least 70% of the trained INITIAL signs show a Harappa start rate of at least 0.40, which with 3 trained signs passes only at 3 of 3.
claims.boundary: The criterion claim (the register's, restated as a definition of the pass line). The share's possible values are 0, 1/3, 2/3, and 1; the 70% bar is met only by 1. It does not govern how a start rate is computed (C10), the zero-occurrence edge (C11), or the unmappable closure (C09), each of which is stated in its own claim.
alternatives: The bar could be read as approximate, or a 2-of-3 result could be reported as substantially meeting it.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 product that reports a 2-of-3 (or lower) share as meeting the criterion, or that applies any bar other than 70% at 0.40, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: The bar could be read as approximate, or a 2-of-3 result could be reported as substantially meeting it.
metadata.verdict_rule: The pass line is 70% of trained signs at start rate 0.40 or above; with 3 signs, only 3 of 3 passes.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C02 defines the pass line; C10 defines the quantity the line applies to (the share of trained signs at or above 0.40). The two are consistent by construction: C10 computes the share C02 judges. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: The cleanliness this design claims is verified training-pool exclusion, not analyst blindness, and the aggregate-inspection disclosure travels with every outcome statement.
claims.boundary: The disclosure claim. The Yajnadevam Harappa pool was inspected in aggregate during the Spec 032 closure audit, and those counts are published (970 Harappa inscriptions inside the old combined training corpus, carrying 1,013 occurrences of 11 of PRED-2026-006's 12 trained signs). No Harappa start rate has ever been computed for any sign. The claim this spec may make is the exclusion re-proven at step 0 (C04); blindness may never be claimed.
alternatives: Because the trained set was derived from CISI data only, the test could be described as a blind holdout test.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 outcome statement describing the test as blind, or omitting the aggregate-inspection disclosure, defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Because the trained set was derived from CISI data only, the test could be described as a blind holdout test.
metadata.verdict_rule: Outcome statements claim verified training-pool exclusion and carry the disclosure; blindness is never claimed.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C07 states what cleanliness may be claimed (exclusion, re-proven); C04 states the act that proves it (the step-0 reproduction). The two are consistent by construction: C07's claim is exactly as strong as C04's check, and neither asserts blindness. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: Sign identity between the trained set and the withheld sequences is carried by the frozen crosswalk only, fixed before counting.
claims.boundary: The identity claim. The mapping is data/crosswalks/yajnadevam_to_parpola_crosswalk.csv under its registered pin (C05); no other mapping, manual match, or judgement call carries a sign's identity. The reading is fixed (DD-035-5): a sign's counterparts are the glyphs whose crosswalk row names it as best_parpola_match - the frozen Phase-396 build's fix_crosswalk reading; top3_parpola alternatives never create a counterpart and set the conflict flag instead. Conflict pairs are flagged in the per-sign table (C12), not resolved by hand. It does not govern the coverage rule (C09), which states what an absent counterpart does.
alternatives: Signs could be matched by visual similarity or expert judgement where the crosswalk is silent.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 product that maps a trained sign to a withheld-sequence sign by any route other than the frozen crosswalk defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Signs could be matched by visual similarity or expert judgement where the crosswalk is silent.
metadata.verdict_rule: The frozen crosswalk is the only identity carrier; it is fixed before counting.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C08 states the crosswalk is the only identity carrier; C09 states the consequence when it carries no counterpart for a trained sign (the unmappable closure). The two are consistent by construction: silence in the sole carrier is exactly the unmappable case. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: Any unmappable trained sign is 33% of the trained set, above the registered 20% cap, and closes the scoring as CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN before the withheld file is opened.
claims.boundary: The coverage claim (spec section 3, check 0.4), in the registration's own terms - stricter than Spec 032's first-sentence coverage statement, because PRED-2026-010's registration declares the closure. The check reads only the crosswalk and the trained set. It does not govern scoring once coverage is complete (C10). Draft-stage observation (spec section 0.4): under the fixed reading (C08), P217 (glyph Y0520) and P324 (glyph Y0740) carry best-match counterparts and P000 carries none - it appears only as a top3_parpola alternative - so the step-0 determination on the pinned bytes is expected to fire this closure. The formal determination remains a step-0 act; the observation is recorded so the freeze decision is informed.
alternatives: An unmappable sign could be dropped from the denominator and the remaining signs scored, as Spec 032's coverage statement allowed.
falsification_tests: A step-0 or scoring record that scores any sign after a trained sign is found unmappable defeats this claim.
A step-0 coverage record showing a best_parpola_match counterpart for P000 on a correct reading of the pinned crosswalk defeats the draft-stage observation recorded in this claim's boundary.

metadata.boundary_confirmation: C09 closes the scoring when coverage is incomplete; C02's criterion judges only a completed scoring. claims.text: The score is the share of trained signs whose Harappa start rate is at least 0.40, a start rate being the share of a sign's Harappa occurrences in the withheld sequences in which it stands in initial position.
claims.boundary: The computation claim (spec section 5). Initial position is the first sign of a sequence, so a one-sign sequence's sign stands initial. The computation runs on the withheld Harappa sequences only, through the frozen crosswalk (C08), after step 0 passes. It does not govern the pass line (C02), the zero-occurrence edge (C11), or any adjustment: none is applied.
alternatives: Start rates could be adjusted for sequence-length composition at Harappa, or computed over all sites rather than Harappa only.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 product whose score uses a different start-rate definition, a different sequence pool, or any composition adjustment defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: Start rates could be adjusted for sequence-length composition at Harappa, or computed over all sites rather than Harappa only.

claims.text: A mappable trained sign with zero Harappa occurrences does not show a start rate at or above 0.40 and counts as not meeting the bar.
claims.boundary: The zero-occurrence edge (spec section 5, DD-035-2), fixed at draft so it cannot be decided after the counts are seen. A sign with no occurrences has no start rate; the registered criterion (C02) credits only signs showing a start rate at or above 0.40. The alternative - closing as not-estimable - is rejected in DD-035-2 because the registered criterion has no such band; the freeze decision may overturn this reading openly. It does not govern unmappable signs (C09), which close the study earlier.
alternatives: A zero-occurrence sign could close the study as not-estimable, or be excluded from the denominator.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 product that credits a zero-occurrence sign toward the share, excludes it from the denominator, or closes as not-estimable on its account defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A zero-occurrence sign could close the study as not-estimable, or be excluded from the denominator.
metadata.verdict_rule: Zero occurrences means the bar is not met for that sign; the denominator stays 3.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C11 governs a mappable sign that occurs zero times; C09 governs a sign with no crosswalk counterpart. The two cases are disjoint - mappability is decided at check 0.4, occurrence counts only exist after scoring opens - and are consistent by construction: a sign cannot be both unmappable and scored-with-zero-occurrences. Neither negates the other.

claims.text: Step-0 closures are reported as themselves, never as verdicts, and a closure is not a refutation of the prediction.
claims.boundary: The closure-reporting claim (spec sections 3 and 6). The closures are CANNOT BE RUN AS WRITTEN (checks 0.2, 0.3, 0.4) and the registration stop (check 0.1). A closed study leaves PRED-2026-010 unscored with Outcome PENDING, and the register's section 4 (Failed Predictions) gains no entry from a closure - the PRED-2026-006 precedent, whose closure is recorded as neither CONFIRMED nor NOT CONFIRMED.
alternatives: A closure could be reported as the prediction failing, since the programme could not run its test.
falsification_tests: Any Spec 035 product that reports a step-0 closure as a verdict, a refutation, or a section 4 entry defeats this claim.

metadata.strongest_rival: A closure could be reported as the prediction failing, since the programme could not run its test.
metadata.verdict_rule: Closures are reported as closures; the prediction's outcome stays PENDING after a closure.
metadata.boundary_confirmation: C15 governs how closures are reported; C02 governs the verdicts of a completed scoring. The two are consistent by construction: a closure means the criterion was never applied, so no verdict exists for C02 to judge and none may be reported. Neither negates the other.
